He changed the style and made it a revelation from Him, as a hint at the strange nature of its affair and the marvel of its condition. So He (exalted) said: ﴿And your Lord revealed﴾, that is, the One who is good to you, by placing honey in the wastelands of the barren deserts, which are extremely bitter, and in other places, and by other benefits, which indicates action by choice and perfect power, ﴿to the bee﴾, that is, through *ilham* (inspiration). Al-Razi said in *Al-Lawami'*: God (exalted) gave every thing its creation and then guided it. Some beings are guided by mere *taskhir* (subjugation), like inanimate things. Some are guided by *ilham* and *taskhir*, like the bee and the *sarfah* (a small creature that builds a house of fine twigs and then enters it and dies there), and the spider. Some are guided by *taskhir*, *ilham*, and an intellect that agrees upon a single order, like the angels. Some are guided by all of that together with thought, discernment, and varied works built upon thought, like man.

Since revelation (*al-iha'*) carries the meaning of speech, He used *an* (the explanatory *an*, *an al-mufassirah*), and said (exalted): ﴿that take for yourselves﴾, that is, do what the one who exerts himself does, namely take ﴿from the mountains houses﴾, what houses! How wondrous they are! ﴿And from the trees﴾, that is, those suitable for that, in the thickets, the mountains, and the deserts, ﴿and from what they build up﴾, that is, what people raise of roofs, walls, and other things. He began with the houses because they are among the wonders of the age in the beauty of craftsmanship, the novelty of form, the excellence of construction, and the perfection of proportion.

(p-198) Since the most important thing for the animal, after rest from the concern of its resting place, is eating, He followed it with that. Since it is general to every fruit, He mentioned it with the particle of delay (*thumma*, "then"), indicating the wondrous craftsmanship in that and the facilitation of it for her. So He (exalted) said: ﴿Then eat﴾. He indicated the abundance of provision by His saying (exalted): ﴿from all the fruits﴾. They said: from subtle particles that fall on the leaves of trees from the shade. Some of them said: from the very flowers and leaves.

Since He had permitted her in all of that, and it is customarily known that obtaining it does not happen except with great hardship in the toil of traveling to it, He drew attention to His breaking of custom in facilitating it for her. So He (exalted) said: ﴿Then follow﴾, meaning: the permission to travel to it follows from the permission to eat. ﴿The ways of your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who benefits you with this great upbringing, for the sake of eating, going to it and returning to your houses, the ways being ﴿smooth﴾, meaning: prepared for travel and facilitated, as He said: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you﴾ [al-Mulk: 15]. By the name "Lord" He indicated that, were it not for His great benevolence in nurturing them, they would not have been guided to that. Then He followed it with its result, in answer to one who might say: "What comes of all this?" So He said (exalted): ﴿There comes forth from their bellies﴾, with a turn of speech, since they did not intend this result, ﴿a drink﴾, what a drink! It is honey, because it, despite being among the finest of foods, is something drunk, ﴿its colours vary﴾ (p-199) between white, red, yellow and other than these, a variation indicating that its Doer, despite complete power, is choosing. Then He clarified that with His saying: ﴿in it﴾, meaning: despite its being among the beneficial fruits and the harmful ones, ﴿is healing for mankind﴾.

Imam al-Razi said in *al-Lawami'*: "Because all compounded medicines are made with honey." Imam of the saints Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: "That was because they humbled themselves to God, being obedient, and ate from all the fruits, the sweet and the bitter, the beloved and the disliked, abandoning their desires. So when they humbled themselves to God's command, this eating became for God, and so it became healing for ailments. Likewise, when the servant humbles himself to God, obeying Him and abandoning his whim, his speech becomes healing for sick hearts." End of quotation.

That it is a healing, in addition to what has been mentioned, is more indicative of power and choice than the variation of colours. Therefore he linked to it His saying (exalted): ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning: in this great matter from all of her affairs, ﴿is a sign﴾. Just as He indicated at the beginning of the verse to the strange craftsmanship in her affairs, He indicated the like of that at the close, by His saying (exalted): ﴿for a people who reflect﴾, meaning: on the bee's being singled out with those fine sciences and hidden subtleties, in houses of hexagonal cells, and its being guided to those subtle particles (p-200) from the tips of trees and leaves, and other marvels. He attached it to thought, which is intensively exercised by the strong, to confirm its grandeur, to magnify its subtlety, and to emphasise its strangeness in indicating perfect knowledge and complete power.

In this surah, the attribution of signs to the addressees has occurred often, sometimes in the singular and sometimes in the plural, and their connection is sometimes to the intellect, sometimes to thought, sometimes to remembrance, and sometimes to other things.

The Divine Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali, in his book *al-Miftah*, made a chapter on this, after having made the teeth of the minds like the teeth of bodies, between discernment, puberty, youth, maturity and other stages, as was previously quoted from him in the surah of *Bara'a* (al-Tawba), at His saying (exalted): ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet﴾ [al-Tawba: 61]. He said: "The ninth chapter concerns the aspects of the attribution of signs and the harmony of states to the teeth of hearts in the Qur'an, that is, for such stages in knowledge and understanding. Know that signs and states are attributed and are in harmony with those who are characterised by that by which they perceive their meaning, and whoever falls short of them is rebuked for them, and their attainment is denied to those who have not reached them. They are stages. The most evident of them (p-201) are the signs of consideration, manifest to people of insight, because all creation is only a sign for consideration from Him, not something existing for being content with it: ﴿And they are content with the life of this world and at rest in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ [Yunus: 7], ﴿Those, their abode is the Fire, because of what they used to earn﴾ [Yunus: 8]. They took what was created for reflection upon its Lord as a gain for themselves, until it became for them and their followers a sign of their own, not a sign of its Creator: ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, in vain?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 128], ﴿And God created you and what you do﴾ [al-Saffat: 96]. Then after the signs of consideration come what is attained by the lower intellect through the immediacy of its sight: ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason﴾ [al-Nahl: 12]. He gathered the signs because their aspects are many in the purpose of clarification. Then after what is perceived by the immediacy of the intellect comes what needs thought that the lower intellect stirs, because the senses are occupied with its benefit away from reflecting on the aspect of its sign: ﴿It is He who sent down from the sky water; from it is drink, and from it are trees in which you pasture﴾ [al-Nahl: 10], ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the palms, the grapes, and of all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect﴾ [al-Nahl: 11]. He made the sign singular because its multiplicity is traced back to the unity of water at the beginning and the unity of benefit at the end. Then after what is perceived by the thought of the lower intellect comes what is accepted (p-202) by faith and is a sign of a command standing upon a creation, and it is perceived by hearing, because creation is seen and command is heard: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ, and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-Nahl: 64], ﴿And God sent down from the sky water and gave life thereby to the earth after its death. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who hear﴾ [al-Nahl: 65]. This is the sign of the life of hearts by the light of knowledge and wisdom, which took hearing at the establishment of faith. At this limit the intellect reaches the innate nature of the strongest, its immediacy rises, and its natures ascend to the consideration of what becomes a sign in the soul of the one who considers, because the hidden realities of existence are returned to the awareness of the observer's deficiency. Just as water is a sign of the life of hearts, the two drinks, milk and wine, have become two signs, upon states that pertain to the hearts, by what God nourishes them with, the nourishment of milk, and what intoxicates them with the intoxication of drunkenness, emerging from between dung and blood, and the descent of the creature from the station of the command upon which it stands: ﴿And indeed in the livestock there is a lesson for you﴾ [al-Nahl: 66], the two signs, up to His saying (exalted): ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason﴾ [al-Nahl: 67]. This is the higher intellect, and He singled out the sign because its place of arrival is singular in the finding of the heart. (p-203) Just as the lower intellect has a thought that reveals its immediacy, so the higher intellect has a thought that reveals the loftiness of its innate nature: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee: take for yourself among the mountains houses, and among the trees﴾ [al-Nahl: 68], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed a sign for a people who reflect﴾. This higher intellect is the core, from which remembrance occurs, through the lower of creation to the higher of command: ﴿And what He has multiplied for you in the earth, its colours varying. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember﴾ [al-Nahl: 13].

Opposite each of these attributes are contraries, and the explanation of them comes according to their contrast. Likewise the ruling on the description of the Muslims therein shows that "there is no salvation for the servant except by submitting himself to his Lord"; and the description of the doers of good, as what appears of the standing of the servant's outward self with his Lord; and the description of the certain, in what the servant finds of certainty in himself, or witnesses its beginning through the outward perception: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ [al-Baqara: 1], ﴿This is the Book, there is no doubt in it, a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqara: 2]. Whoever is content with what he has of finding is not free to accept the unseen: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger﴾ [al-Hadid: 28], ﴿When they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Him and believe, then fear Him and do good﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 93], ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85], ﴿Then they feared God and did good, and God loves the good-doers﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 93]. (p-204) (*"When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees"*). ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain﴾ [al-Jathiya: 4], ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75].

For the totality of these attributes there are also contraries, in which the explanation of the Qur'an comes according to their opposition, and its understanding flows with them. What the deafness of hearing and the blindness of sight could not bring to the heart is its understanding, and whoever lacks that has his hearing described as deaf, his eye as blind, his heart as devoid of understanding, and is attributed to animality. Whoever does not attain by his thought the knowledge of what his sight has not witnessed is denied knowledge: ﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance, and they were not able to hear﴾ [al-Kahf: 101], ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock, rather they are more astray; those are the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], ﴿They say: "If we return to Medina..."﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], up to His saying: ﴿But the hypocrites do not know﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], ﴿They say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse"﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], the verse, up to His saying (exalted): ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7]. Knowledge is denied concerning what its signs are manifest, and understanding concerning what its matter is hidden. The intended explanation of their opposites, these attributes according to their contrast, and this chapter is among the most beneficial openings of understanding in the Qur'an for one who begins it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 70:

When He had roused them from their slumber and alerted them to the gravity of their heedlessness regarding the all-encompassing power and the comprehensive knowledge, which necessitate acting by choice and which establish the resurrection and other things, of everything that He - glorified is He - wills, through some of His signs spread across the horizons, from the inanimate and then the animal, and He concluded that with what is a cure, He followed it with some of the proofs in their own selves for that, reminding them of the four stages of the human lifespan: the age of childhood and growth; then the age of youth, at whose end comes standing (at the peak); then the age of middle age (kuhulah), in which decline begins while strength remains; then the age of decline with the appearance of weakness, which is old age (shaykhukhah), including what no medicine can avert, urging reflection upon His signs and understanding them before that event occurs, lest the opportunity be lost and they regret where regret does not benefit, He said: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge; ﴿created you﴾, making you, after non-existence, living, knowing, and disputing; ﴿then He causes you to die﴾, according to the differing ages, so the young cannot delay it, nor can the old advance it; so among you is one who dies while at the height of his strength; ﴿and among you is one who is returned﴾, that is, by the easiest command from Us, which he cannot resist in any way; ﴿to the most abject age﴾, because he becomes senile, returning to a state like that of childhood in weakness, with others loathing him, and no hope remains after it; ﴿so that he will not know﴾. Since the purpose of the surah is to demonstrate the perfection of power, the comprehensiveness of knowledge, and the transcendence above every trace of deficiency, and since the context here is also for that, as evidenced by the ending of the verse, he removed the preposition to indicate that ignorance encompasses the period after knowledge, so it connects with death, against which no medicine benefits and no stratagem avails. Thus He said: ﴿after having known, anything﴾; nothing of that, when it descends, is found to have a cure, nor does medicine prevent it. So hasten to reflection and consideration before one of these two befalls you. Then He justified that by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassment; ﴿is Knowing, Competent﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge and all-encompassing power; so whatever He wills, it is; and whatever others will but He does not will, His knowledge encompasses it, and by His power He causes what prevents it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 71:

When he had mentioned the variation in lifespans, which proclaims the nullification of natures and obliges a race to take heed for those with insight, so that they fear every moment the calamity of death, he followed it with the variation in provisions. He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs, (p-207) ﴿has favoured some of you﴾, O people, ﴿over others﴾. Since the aspects of favouring are many, and since favouring in livelihood, which a person thinks he has some power to obtain, and whose variation is more indicative of the completeness of power and of acting by choice (the very thing the context is about), He said: ﴿in provision﴾. That is: indeed He may make the weak, incapable, ignorant one richer than the strong, cunning, knowledgeable one. So fear Allah, act with moderation in seeking, and turn all your hearts to what benefits you of insight.

Abu Nu'aym said in al-Hilya: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Amr al-Khallal narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn Abi 'Umar say: We were with Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, and they mentioned al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi' and his cleverness, so Sufyan began to recite:

؎ How many a strong man is strong in his turning, ∗∗∗ whose sound judgment is refined, yet provision turns away from him.

؎ And how many a weak one, feeble of intellect and confused, ∗∗∗ as if he were scooping from the gulf of the sea.

It is related from the Nawadir of Abu 'Ali al-Qali that he said: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said: and my father narrated to me, (p-208) that Sulayman al-Muhallabi sent al-Khalil ibn Ahmad one hundred thousand dirhams and asked him for his companionship; so he returned the hundred thousand and wrote to him these verses:

؎ Tell Sulayman that I am, regarding him, in ease, ∗∗∗ and in richness, though I am not a man of wealth.

؎ I am content in myself that I do not see anyone ∗∗∗ dying of hunger, nor remaining in one state.

؎ Provision comes by decree; weakness does not diminish it, ∗∗∗ nor does the scheming of a schemer increase it for you.

؎ Poverty is in the soul, not in wealth, you know it, ∗∗∗ and likewise richness is in the soul, not in wealth.

Since making the owned equal in rank to the owner is something that greatly offends them regarding their rights—even though in reality there is no ownership or sovereignty for the slave—so they do not submit to it, nor is it submitted to them, even if the matter is grave and leads to the loss of lives; rather, whoever's mother was a slave, they lower his rank, even if his father was who he was; and although the consideration among them in (p-209) lineage is by the father, this is what compelled 'Antara to say:

؎ I am a man of the noblest lineage among 'Abs, ∗∗∗ my half, and I defend the rest with the blade,

and to other things of the kind that he used to excuse himself for on his mother's side. He (glorified is He) alerted them to what they had fallen into regarding His right through this, by way of associating partners with Him, although He is the Owner of the Kingdom and the King of kings, after they had dared against Him in preferring themselves in attributing daughters to Him. So He said: ﴿Then those who have been favoured﴾, that is, in provision, ﴿will not give back their provision﴾, that is, which they have been singled out with, ﴿to what their right hands possess﴾, even if their benefit is great and their station weighty in their eyes, ﴿so that they are equal in it﴾, that is, by that return the owner and the owned become equal. This is the answer to the negation, as transmitted by al-Rammal from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada, may Allah be pleased with them.

When this became clear as the sun, and appeared such that there was not at all any kind of ambiguity, the denunciation resulted from it in His saying—in a manner of turning away from addressing them, which signals abhorrence: ﴿Then is it the favour of Allah﴾, that is, the One besides whom there is no lord, ﴿that they deny?﴾ in their making for Him partners to whom they ascribe some of what He has bestowed upon them, thereby equating themselves with Him in that; and it is for their favour that they acknowledge and guard, by bringing down what their right hands possess from them in ranks and wealth.

When he mentioned creation and provision, he followed them with the delights of finding companionship in one's own kind through spouses, children, and other things, which are necessary for the upkeep of one's interests. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses perfect power and complete knowledge, ﴿has made for you﴾. Since spouses are of the same kind, He said: ﴿from your own selves﴾, because a thing is more at ease with its own type and closer to its own kind, ﴿spouses﴾; that is, you reproduce through them, and finding tranquility in them becomes a means of preserving your species. ﴿And has made for you﴾; that is, O people, who direct your desires to other than Him, ﴿from your spouses, sons﴾. Perhaps He placed them first for their nobility. Then He joined to this what is more general, saying: ﴿and grandchildren (ḥafadah)﴾; that is, from the daughters and sons, their children, and in-laws and relatives by marriage. Ḥafadah is the plural of ḥāfid, who are light and quick in your affairs and swift in serving you, out of obedience and loyalty, unlike strangers and some undutiful persons. This is the meaning of what al-Rummani transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them), that he interpreted them as servants and helpers, and this is the correct view, because the root ḥ-f-d (ḥafada) revolves around speed and lightness. ḥafada (حَفَدَ): he was light in work and quick. al-ḥafad (الحَفَدُ), with vowelling as ḥaraka: servants, because of their lightness, and a gait below the khabab (a fast trot). al-ḥafadah (الحَفَدَةُ): daughters, grandchildren, or in-laws for this reason, and embroiderers, because of their speed in it, and the speed of the wearer in putting on a garment with an untroubled mind. al-mahfid (المَحْفِدُ), on the pattern of majlis and minbar: a place where animals are fed, because of their hastening to it; and on the pattern of minbar: the edge of a garment, because of the quickness of its movement; and a vessel used for measuring, because of its lightness; and on the pattern of majlis: the origin, because affairs revolve around it and hasten toward it. Sayf muḥtafid (سَيْفٌ مُحْتَفِدٌ): a sword swift in cutting. Aḥfadahu (أحْفَدَهُ): he compelled him to hasten. al-fādiḥah (الفادِحَةُ): a calamity that befalls; fawadiḥ al-dahr (فَوادِحُ الدَّهْرِ): the misfortunes of time, because they hasten with what is disliked, and the one upon whom they fall hastens to repel them, and the one who is concerned with his affair hastens to repel them. From this is fadahahu al-amr (فَدَحَهُ الأمْرُ): the matter burdened him, because the disliked thing hastens and weighs heavily, so the agitation of the one upon whom it falls increases.

When He (glorified is He) had mentioned this, He followed it with what life is not good without, and so He (exalted is He) said: ﴿and provided for you﴾; that is, to sustain your needs and to set right your conditions. Since all bliss is only in Paradise, He made it partial, saying: ﴿of the good things﴾, by making it agreeable to natures, delightful to souls, and beneficial for nourishment. From this it is known with certainty that the doer of these actions is the One specially possessed of majesty, and whoever denies any part of His right has strayed into the furthest error. How much more so, then, is one who denies His goodness and worships other than Him, while He is more deserving of the name of existence than they are of the name of nonexistence! Therefore, his saying followed from this, turning away from addressing them with the aversion of one who is angry: ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood﴾; that is, in the idols and what they assigned to them as a share; ﴿believe﴾; that is, in a manner of renewal and continuity. ﴿And in the favor of Allah﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 67]; that is, the Supreme King, ﴿they﴾, while He has especially upon them, beyond what they share with people, favors that belong to Him, ﴿disbelieve﴾. To the extent that they assign to their idols part of what He has bestowed upon them, such as the sa'ibah, the waṣilah, the ḥām, and others. This includes ingratitude for the blessing that comes from Him, and includes attributing it to another, because He had not permitted them anything of what they forbade, and the disposal of the property of its owner is not lawful except with his permission.

Then He said, coordinating with what He had denounced them for there: ﴿And they worship﴾; and He pointed to the lowness of all ranks removed from His own exalted station, glorified is He, saying (exalted is He): ﴿besides Allah﴾; that is, besides the One who possesses majesty and honour, [they worship] that which is at the utmost lowness, namely idols and others; ﴿that which possesses not﴾; that is, in any respect whatsoever; ﴿for them any provision﴾; abandoning the One in whose hand is all provision, and who is the Possessor of absolute exaltedness, who provided them with good things. Then He specified the source of the provision, saying (exalted is He): ﴿from the heavens and the earth﴾. Then He emphasized the generality of this negation by His saying, substituting it for "provision" and making clear that its tanwin is for belittling: ﴿anything﴾. Then He emphasized their worthlessness by His saying, gathering [the two], because what is incapable when gathered is even more incapable when alone: ﴿and they have no power﴾; that is, they have no kind of power at all. And you may make it coordinated with what preceded of the matters of wonder concerning their statements and actions, in His saying: "and they assign to Allah what they dislike," and the like.

When He refuted with this argument all the doubts they had raised, and the parables they had coined in the claims they had committed themselves to, namely their saying that the king cannot be reached except through helpers, such as a chamberlain, a deputy and the like, and cannot be approached except by various kinds of offerings, they worshipped idols and did for them what is done for Him, likening Him, exalted is His majesty and sublime is His dominion. The difference is that the earthly kings, to whom they were comparing Him, only appointed such helpers because of their own need and the weakness of their rule and possession. Their situation is therefore contrary to the description of the One whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, whom no affair distracts from another, and to whom everything is subject and under His dominion and majesty. Because of this, there followed His saying (exalted is He): ﴿So do not strike parables for God﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassing knowledge, ﴿the parables﴾, that is, by likening Him to others in comparison with something else, even though He Himself strikes parables for you. Abu Hayyan and others said: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: that is, do not liken Him to His creation. End of quotation. As al-Kashshaf says, this is an illustration of associating partners with Allah and likening Him to others, because whoever strikes parables likens one state to another state and one story to another story. End of quotation. This prohibition is general to every parable, because of the gravity of the matter, lest that parable be unworthy of His station. It has been established that averting harms takes precedence over securing benefits, especially in this matter, because error in it is disbelief. This is indicated by the grounding of the ruling in His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs and to whom no one else has any command, ﴿knows﴾ [p. 215] that is, He possesses the entirety of the attribute of knowledge. So when He strikes a parable, He perfects it through the encompassing of His knowledge, such that no one other than Him can show any difference between the one who is likened and that to which it is likened, in the matter being illustrated. ﴿And you do not know﴾, that is, you have no knowledge at all, and therefore you are blinded to the sun, and what is free of confusion becomes confused for you. This station is elevated, its path is rugged, and whoever travels it is in a state of great peril.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 75:

When He, glory be to Him, concluded that matter, to confirm the refutation of the doctrine of the idol-worshippers by denying them knowledge, which is the basis of rectitude (*sadad*), it was fitting that He join to it His statement, as proof of His knowledge that such similitudes are not open to criticism and that doubts do not turn toward them: ﴿God strikes a parable﴾, that is, He who possesses perfect knowledge and complete power, ﴿a parable﴾ concerning free persons and slaves, regarding Himself and what you worship alongside Him. Then He substituted (*ibdal*) for "a parable" the words ﴿a slave﴾. Since the word "slave" (*'abd*) is applied to a free person in relation to God (exalted is He), He said ﴿owned﴾, not a *mukatab* (a slave contracted to purchase his freedom), and not one who has any trace of freedom. ﴿He has no power over anything﴾, neither by the permission of his master nor by anyone else's. This is the parable of their associates. Then He coordinated (*'atf*) upon "a slave" the statement ﴿and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us﴾, that is, from among the free, ﴿good provision﴾, abundant and pure, ﴿so he spends from it﴾ constantly. This is the meaning of ﴿secretly and openly﴾. This is the parable of God, and to Him belongs the highest similitude. Then He rebuked them in denial with His statement, exalted is He: (p-216) ﴿Are they equal?﴾, that is, these two groups represented by the parable, because the intended meaning is the category. If it is not sound in reason to equate two created beings, one of whom is free and capable and the other a owned slave who is powerless, how then can a dead stone or something else be equated with God, to whom belongs complete power over everything?

Since the answer is definitively "No," and it is known that the superior one is not a likeness of Him, glory be to Him, and since whoever equates the two or does what leads to equality is among the most ignorant of the ignorant.

Thus the content of ﴿Indeed, God knows, and you do not know﴾ is established, and that anything other than Him, exalted is He, is worth nothing. It is therefore established beyond doubt that He alone is entitled to the highest similitude. He expressed this by His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to God﴾, that is, to Him belongs the comprehensive knowledge and all the attributes of perfection, among which is that He alone is entitled to thanks, because He is the Bestower of blessings. No one else has any comprehension of any of that, nor of anything else. It is as if they had said: "We know this," so it was said: ﴿Rather, most of them﴾, that is, apparently and inwardly (indicated by the pronoun), ﴿do not know﴾, because they equate others with Him. Whoever denies Him knowledge, which is the highest of the attributes of perfection, is counted among the cattle. Therefore they liken to Him what has been mentioned, strike false parables, and attribute His blessings to what cannot be counted. Perhaps He used the third-person pronoun to restrict this to those who died in misguidance. Or it may be said, and this is more elegant: since the answer is definitively "They are not equal," and the superior one is your likeness, every person of understanding knows that You have the highest similitude. Thus He expressed His description (p-217) by the statement ﴿Praise be to God﴾, that is, the comprehensive possession of the attributes of perfection belongs to the Supreme King, and He expressed their attribution of knowledge of this by ﴿but most of them do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge of anything at all, because in this matter they act out of ignorance. Therefore, to attribute to them heedlessness is better, in regard to them, than to attribute to them misguidance with knowledge. What will be beneficial in this context will come, God willing, in surah Luqman.

The word *al-ḥamd* has been explained as above because it has already been stated in surah al-Fatiha that the root *ḥ-m-d* (ḥamida) revolves around reaching the ultimate limit (*ghāya*), and this entails expansion, comprehensiveness, and circularity, and so it entails the lowering of the head. The ultimate limit may also entail contentment, and so it entails gratitude. Its explanation: *al-ḥamd* means contentment and gratitude, since both generally arise from the ultimate limit of beneficence. From this root come the meanings "recompense," "fulfilment of a right," *ḥumādāk* (with a *ḍamma*), meaning your ultimate limit; *yawmun muḥtamid*, a day of intense heat; *ḥamad al-nār* (with vowelling), the sound of a fire blazing. As for *yatahammad 'alayya*, meaning "he bestows favour upon me," its origin is that he mentions what necessarily entails praising him. From it comes *al-madḥ*, which is good praise. *Tamaddaḥa*, meaning he strove to praise and boasted and pretended to have what he does not have, for in all of that he has exerted his effort. *Dahamahu*, like *manaʿa*, means he pushed him forcefully. *Al-mar'a*, meaning he married her, because in that there is reaching the ultimate limit of desire and what necessarily follows of pushing and the like. *Al-diḥm*, with a kasra, means the origin, because it is the ultimate limit of the thing to which it leads. *Ḥadm al-nār*, and it may be vowelled, means the intensity of its burning and its heat. *Iḥtadama al-dam* means the blood's redness intensified until it turned black. *Al-ḥadama*, vowelled, means fire, because it is the ultimate limit of heat. *Al-ḥadama* also means its sound, because it indicates the strength of its blazing. From this also comes *al-ḥadama*, for the sound from the belly of a snake, or a sound within the belly, as if it were anger, because it indicates the ultimate limit of the inner blaze. *Al-ḥadma*, like *farḥa*, is a pot that boils quickly. From expansion comes *tamaddaḥat al-arḍ*, that is, the land expanded. From circularity comes *al-dāḥūm*, the snare of the fox, because it has reached the ultimate limit of the hunter's aim, and because when it cannot escape from it, it is as if it had encompassed it. *Al-daḥmaḥ* means round and compact, and *daḥaḥa, tadmīḥan*, means he lowered his head, because bending is the starting point of circularity. And God, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Granter of success.

ولَمّا انْقَضى هَذا المَثَلُ كافِيًا في المُرادِ؛ مُلْزِمًا لَهم لِاعْتِرافِهِمْ بِأنَّ الأصْنامَ عَبِيدُ اللَّهِ؛ في قَوْلِهِمْ: ”لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ؛ لا شَرِيكَ لَكَ؛ (p-219) إلّا شَرِيكًا هو لَكَ؛ تَمْلِكُهُ وما مَلَكَ“؛ وكانَ رُبَّما كابَرَ مُكابِرٌ فَقالَ: إنَّهم لَيْسُوا مِلْكًا لَهُ؛ أتْبَعَهُ مَثَلًا آخَرَ؛ لا تُمْكِنُ المُكابَرَةُ فِيهِ؛ فَقالَ (تَعالى): ﴿وضَرَبَ اللَّهُ﴾؛ أيْ: الَّذِي لَهُ الإحاطَةُ الكامِلَةُ أيْضًا؛ ﴿مَثَلا﴾؛ ثُمَّ أبْدَلَ مِنهُ ﴿رَجُلَيْنِ﴾ (badal: substitution, here an appositive restating the preceding noun); ثُمَّ اسْتَأْنَفَ البَيانَ لِما أجْمَلَ؛ فَقالَ (تَعالى): ﴿أحَدُهُما أبْكَمُ﴾؛ أيْ: وُلِدَ أخْرَسَ؛ ثُمَّ تَرْجَمَ بُكْمَتَهُ الَّتِي أُرِيدَ بِها أنَّهُ لا يَفْهَمُ؛ ولا يُفْهِمُ؛ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾؛ أيْ: أصْلًا؛ ﴿وهُوَ كَلٌّ﴾؛ أيْ: ثِقْلٌ؛ وعِيالٌ؛ والأصْلُ فِيهِ الغِلَظُ؛ الَّذِي يَمْنَعُ مِنَ النُّفُوذِ؛ ”كَلَّتِ السِّكِّينُ كُلُولًا“؛ إذا غَلُظَتْ شَفْرَتُها؛ فَلَمْ تَقْطَعْ؛ و”كَلَّ لِسانُهُ“؛ إذا لَمْ يَنْبَعِثْ في القَوْلِ؛ لِغِلَظِهِ وذَهابِ حَدِّهِ؛ قالَهُ الرُّمّانِيُّ (al-Rummani); ﴿عَلى مَوْلاهُ﴾؛ الَّذِي يَلِي أمْرَهُ؛ ثُمَّ بَيَّنَ ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ (تَعالى): ﴿أيْنَما يُوَجِّهْهُ﴾؛ أيْ: يُرْسِلْهُ؛ ويَصْرِفْهُ؛ ذَلِكَ المَوْلى؛ ﴿لا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ﴾؛ وهَذا مَثَلُ شُرَكائِهِمُ الَّذِينَ هم عِيالٌ؛ ووَبالٌ عَلى عَبَدَتِهِمْ.

(p-220) ولَمّا انْكَشَفَ ضَلالُهم في تَسْوِيَتِهِمُ الأنْدادَ - الَّذِينَ لا قُدْرَةَ لَهم عَلى شَيْءٍ ما - بِاللَّهِ؛ الَّذِي لَهُ الإحاطَةُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قُدْرَةً وعِلْمًا؛ حَسُنَ كُلَّ الحُسْنِ تَوْبِيخُهُمْ؛ والإنْكارُ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ بِقَوْلِهِ (تَعالى): ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ﴾؛ أيْ: هَذا المَذْكُورُ؛ ﴿ومَن﴾؛ أيْ: ورَجُلٌ آخَرُ عَلى ضِدِّ صِفَتِهِ؛ فَهو عالِمٌ؛ فَطِنٌ؛ قَوِيٌّ؛ خَبِيرٌ؛ مُبارَكُ الأمْرِ؛ مَيْمُونُ النَّقِيبَةِ؛ ﴿يَأْمُرُ﴾؛ بِما لَهُ مِنَ العِلْمِ؛ والقُدْرَةِ؛ ﴿بِالعَدْلِ﴾؛ أيْ: بِبَذْلِ النَّصِيحَةِ لِغَيْرِهِ؛ ﴿وهُوَ﴾؛ في نَفْسِهِ؛ ظاهِرًا وباطِنًا؛ ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ﴾؛ أيْ: طَرِيقٍ واضِحٍ؛ واسِعٍ؛ ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾؛ أيْ: عامِلٌ بِما يَأْمُرُ بِهِ؛ وهَذا مِثالٌ لِلْمَعْبُودِ بِالحَقِّ؛ الَّذِي يَكْفِي عابِدَهُ جَمِيعَ المُؤَنِ؛ وهو دالٌّ عَلى كَمالِ عِلْمِهِ؛ وتَمامِ قُدْرَتِهِ.

When these two parables were complete, both indicating the perfection of His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His power, and both establishing that anything other than Him is non-existent, He followed His saying "Indeed, Allah knows" with His saying, explicitly stating the perfection of His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His power: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, this is Allah's knowledge of what is witnessed, which, from these proofs, is known to be exclusive to Him, and to the Possessor of Majesty and Honour alone. ﴿The unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, just as to Him alone belongs their witnessing. Whatever He wills from that, His power over it is like His power over the witnessing of the Hour, which you deny out of considering it great. And [He also has power over] other than these two, by what He has detailed for you from the beginning of the surah until here, of the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them. ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as the blink of an eye﴾. The Hour is the time in which the Resurrection occurs, which you believe will not happen, considering it far-fetched and regarding its matter as difficult, although in its speed, if people were to see it, [it would be swift]. For this reason it was expressed as "the Hour." ﴿Or it is nearer﴾: that is, like the return of the glance, attributed to the sight, whatever sight it may be. ﴿Or it is nearer﴾, and suddenly the creatures will have risen from their graves, hastening toward the caller. This is with respect to their knowledge and their measurement. As for with respect to Him, glory be to Him, His command in its majesty, greatness, speed and perfection is too exalted to be described, and minds fall short of it. There is no doubt about it and no hesitation. For this reason He gave the reason for it with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿is over all things﴾, that is, all that is possible, ﴿Competent﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 78:

When his rebuke of them for their belief in falsehood and their disbelief in the truth, and what follows from that, had come to an end, and he concluded with the matter of the Hour, he linked to his saying (exalted is He): "And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves" (16:72) what is among the proofs of the Hour, of the completeness of power, and of acting by choice, from the first creation. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs all greatness (p-222) ﴿brought you forth﴾ by His knowledge and power ﴿from the wombs of your mothers﴾; and the One who brought you forth from them is capable of bringing you forth from the belly of the earth, without any difference, rather all the more so; while you, at the time of emergence, ﴿know nothing﴾ of things, be they few or many. He linked to "brought you forth" his saying: ﴿and made for you﴾, likewise by that, ﴿hearing, sight and hearts﴾ as instruments to remove the ignorance upon which birth occurred. He opened their places and shaped them, arranged them and balanced them while you were in the bellies, where no hand can reach them and no one can cut any part of them with an instrument. So the One who was able to do that in the bellies by origination is capable of restoring it in the belly of the earth, rather all the more so. Perhaps He combined them (sight and hearing), leaving out hearing, because the variation in them is greater than the variation in hearing, by a degree known only to Allah. And "the hearts" (al-af'idah) are the hearts, which He prepared for understanding and the correction of the body, by the subtle warmth He deposited in them, which is receptive to subtle meanings. ﴿So that you may give thanks﴾; that is, so that you may become, through the knowledge of the hearts which He bestowed upon you, when you hear the admonitions and see the signs, in a state in which your thanks is hoped for, since He has bestowed upon you of the subtleties of His workmanship, by coming to know what He possesses of knowledge, power and goodness of perception, and so you acknowledge to Him all that His messengers have brought you. Most important (p-223) of it, upon which all the aims of the fundamentals are built, is that the One who bestows these blessings upon you is one God, knowing of everything, capable of everything, acting by choice; and that natures are among the things He has power over, having no action of their own except by His direction.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 79:

Since the purpose of enumerating these blessings is to inform (the reader) that He alone is the Agent by (His) choice, not the natures (tabā'i') nor anything else, He guided them to this through a matter that is implied by what preceded, by His saying, confirming it for them: ﴿Have they not seen﴾; with the address (khiṭāb) and with the third person (ghayba), according to the difference of the two readings; because the context (siyāq) and the preceding discourse (sibāq) of the speech admit both the one addressed and the one turning away, unlike the context of Surat al-Mulk, which is for the one turning away only; therefore the reciters differed here, and agreed there. ﴿At the birds, made subservient﴾; that is, made subdued for flying, by what Allah has established in them of benefits and wisdoms, for flying and other than it; ﴿in the air of the sky﴾; in the atmosphere, between the two horizons, in a manner that you are not able to do in any way, despite your sharing with them in hearing and sight, and your superiority over them through intellects. Thus it is known with certainty what was connected to this by His saying: ﴿None holds them up﴾; that is, in the air from falling.

Since the context here has a great bearing on refuting the people of natures, who are the philosophers, and they have a great influence on people's hearts, He expressed (Himself) with the Greatest Name, indicating that none is able to refute their doubts except one who has comprehensive knowledge of the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names, and so is firmly established in the knowledge of the foundations of religion (uṣūl al-dīn). So He said: ﴿except Allah﴾; that is, the Greatest King; because your relation and theirs to nature is one, so if that were its action, you would be equal (to the birds). Then He alerted them to the wisdoms in that by His saying: ﴿Indeed in that﴾; that is, in this great matter, of bringing you forth in that form, and bestowing upon you what they do not have, and ordaining for you what you were not able to do despite their being inferior to you; ﴿are signs﴾; and since whoever does not benefit from a thing is as if he did not possess it, He (Exalted) said: ﴿for a people who believe﴾; that is, the Chooser Agent has prepared them for faith.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 80:

When He (Glory be to Him) reminded them of the blessing of perception, after the beginning of creation, and followed it with what He bestowed upon the birds by way of elevation, which protects them from the heat, He followed that with what they dwell in and take shelter in, and which gathers them together, because it is the most important of things for living creatures. So He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses perfect wisdom and all-encompassing power, ﴿has made for you﴾, that is, O heedless ones, ﴿from your houses﴾. The origin of "bayt" (house) is a shelter for the night; then its usage was extended. ﴿A place of rest﴾ is a verbal noun used in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul), meaning a place in which one rests. He did not give power over you in them to insects and wild beasts, as He gave you power over them. Then He followed what is specific to the settled life with what is suitable for travel, through what distinguished them from the birds and the rest of the animals. So He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And He has made for you﴾, that is, as a favour to you, ﴿from the hides of cattle﴾, which He has made subject to you.

When the tents made from the hides of cattle, in their wide shade, approach the dwellings of villages, He gathered them in the plural, saying: ﴿houses﴾. For they said: this plural form (buyut) is more specific to dwellings made of solid material, while "abyat" (tents) is more specific to those made of hair. ﴿You find them light⁠—﴾, that is, you seek to make them light by construction, and you find them thus, ﴿on the day of your journeying﴾, that is, at the time of your departure, and He expressed it with "day" because it is mostly in daytime, ﴿and on the day of your settling﴾. Then He followed this with what completes the comfort of dwelling, so He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And from their wool﴾, that is, of sheep from among them, ﴿and their fur﴾, which for camels is like wool for sheep, ﴿and their hair﴾, which is what comes from goats and the like, ﴿[provide] household goods﴾, that is, a great deal of furnishings from the household goods, for dwellings, clothing, bedding, tent coverings and other things, ﴿and a provision﴾, which you enjoy, ﴿for a time﴾, that is, for an unspecified time, according to each person's loss of it. He turned away from mentioning silk, linen and cotton, because these were not among their crafts, and as an indication of moderation and avoidance of extravagance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 81:

When He had mentioned what is specific to them, He followed it with what they share with the rest of the animals. So He said: ﴿And Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs majesty and generosity; ﴿has made for you﴾; that is, without any need on His part, glory be to Him; ﴿of what He has created, shade﴾; from trees, mountains, and other things; ﴿and He has made for you﴾; that is, despite His absolute independence; ﴿among the mountains, shelters﴾; the plural of "kinn," which is that by which one takes shelter; that is, one is concealed, from caves and the like. Had the Creator not been one who chooses, they would have been of one uniform course, with no shade and no shelters. Then He followed this with what He guided them to, as a substitute for what He had given to the rest of the animals, so He said: ﴿And He has made for you﴾; that is, as a favour from Him to you; ﴿garments [sarabil]﴾; that is, clothes; ﴿that protect you from the heat﴾; and these are every thing worn, such as a shirt and other things, as al-Zajjaj said.

Since the garments [sarabil] were one kind, He did not repeat "made" (ja'ala), so He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And garments [sarabil]﴾; that is, coats of mail, helmets, and other things; ﴿that protect you against your violence﴾. He attributed it to them to convey that it is war; and this is like what He made for the rest of the animals, of wool and the like, and of fangs and claws and the like, which is similar to that, preventing (p-227) heat, cold, and the weapons of the enemy. He (glory be to Him) did not mention here the protection from cold, because it was mentioned earlier in His saying (exalted is He): "for you therein is warmth." When this was complete, it was as though it were said: He, glory be to Him, has alerted us with this statement to the completion of the blessing of bringing into existence; so is there any blessing after it? He said: Yes; ﴿thus﴾; that is, just as He completed for you the blessing of bringing into existence with this great completion through these matters, and alerted you to them; ﴿He completes His blessing upon you﴾; in this world and in religion, by guidance, by making clear the path of salvation, by benefits, and by drawing attention to the subtle details of these after the grand ones; ﴿that you may submit﴾; that is, so that your state, in view of the abundance of His beneficence that no one else can bring about, with the matter being so clear, becomes the state of one from whom submission of his will to his Lord is hoped for; so he neither rests nor moves except in obedience to Him.

Thus, when this explanation became clearer than direct witnessing, it might have occurred to the mind that if they did not respond, distress would befall the one calling (to the truth) because of their turning away. So He (exalted is He), negating that and turning away from them with the turning away of one who is angry, and turning toward him (p-228) — may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace — with the turning of one who consoles, expressing it with the form "tafa''ul" (the reflexive/causative verbal pattern), which conveys that the original natural disposition (al-fitar al-ula) calls toward turning to Allah; so its possessor does not turn away from what pleases Him — glory be to Him — except through some kind of treatment: ﴿But if they turn away﴾; that is: they burden themselves with turning away and with following their desires; so there is no shortcoming upon you because of their turning away, nor any distress. ﴿Then indeed﴾; that is: because it is only ﴿upon you is the clear conveyance﴾; and it is not upon you to turn them back from obstinacy.

It is as if it were said: "Was their turning away out of ignorance or out of obstinacy?" So it was said about them, and among them: ﴿they recognise﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿the favour of Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, ﴿which was previously enumerated in part in this surah and elsewhere﴾, ﴿then they deny it﴾, either by worshipping other than the One who bestows it, or by denying the one who came to draw attention to it. Some of them did so because of weak knowledge, and some out of obstinacy. Some of them used to say: "It is from Allah, but through the intercession of our gods." ﴿And most of them﴾, that is, of those addressed, in relation to all the people of the earth, those reached by his call (ﷺ), ﴿are the disbelievers﴾, that is, the obstinate, those firmly established in disbelief.

(p-229) Since among the greatest purposes of these methods is warning against the Resurrection, and it is known that after turning away from clear proof and persisting in ingratitude for the favour one has been shown, nothing remains but requital, because the Wise grants respite but does not neglect, He (exalted is He) said, linking it to the outcome of ﴿Your duty is only to convey the clear message﴾, which is: so convey to them, make it clear to them, and do not despair of their returning:

﴿And [warn them of] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾; i.e., warn them of the Day when We raise up, after the raising (of the dead), from every nation a witness, who will testify by his word, the King (judging) so that the matter proceeds in accordance with what they are accustomed to, even though He is free of need for any witness. Since permission for them to offer excuses during the long stages of that Day was impossible, He (glory be to Him) expressed this with the particle of distance and said (exalted is He): ﴿Then no leave will be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be asked to make amends﴾; i.e., no granting of leave takes place, under any of the possible assumptions, for those who disbelieved, after the testimony of the witnesses, to offer excuses, as leave is granted in this world to one who is accused when questioned about his excuse; for in reality there is no excuse there. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾; i.e., nor will they be asked for the (kind of) appeasement that brings about contentment, which is the removal of displeasure, the displeasure being what is expressed by anger, which in turn is expressed through its effects of force, retribution, and the seizing of punishment upon the people of criminality, because of the evil of what they committed; because that abode is not a place of obligation.

Then he connected to it that what anger necessitates persists upon them on that day. So He (Exalted) said, coordinating with what follows "then" (p-230): ﴿And when those who wronged see﴾. He stated the apparent noun in place of the pronoun for generality, saying ﴿those who wronged﴾, thereby expressing them by the attribute that necessitates punishment, ﴿the punishment﴾, after the standing (before the Lord) and the testimony of the witnesses. The conditional's response is omitted, indicated by what is connected to the agency (fa'iliyyah), its estimated form being: "it overtakes them." ﴿So it will not be lightened﴾, meaning: no lightening will occur by any kind of means, nor by anyone of creation, ﴿for them﴾, any part of it; ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, by postponement, nor even for a moment, in any manner, under any estimation, from anyone whatsoever.

When Allah, glorified is He, had explained the outcome of their affair in the resurrection and what follows it, and since among the most important matters was their situation at the place of standing (al-mawqif) with their associates whom they used to hope in, He linked to that His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And when those who associated [others with Allah] see their associates﴾; that is, with their own eyes, on the Day of Resurrection; ﴿those who associated﴾; so He also mentioned the description appropriate to the situation; ﴿their associates﴾; that is, the deities which they used to call associates; ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our associates, whom we used to call upon besides You."﴾ They attributed them to themselves, because there is no reality to their partnership except their naming them so, which brought about their harm. Then they clarified what they meant by their saying: ﴿whom we used to call upon﴾; that is, worship.

Since the ranks are many beneath His rank (glorified is He), for His exaltedness is not confined, He introduced the preposition and said (exalted is He): ﴿besides You﴾; so that they might bring us near to You; so honor us for their sake, (p-231) following their way in this world in ignorance and dullness. The associates feared the consequences of this statement and of acknowledging it, the assaults of anger; ﴿So they will throw at them﴾; that is, the associates; ﴿to them﴾; that is, the polytheists; ﴿the statement﴾; that is, they hastened with it, until their hastening toward them was like the hastening of a heavy thing thrown down from a height. They emphasized their statement, because it is a refutation of the polytheists' claim, so they said: ﴿Indeed, you are liars﴾; in our being made associates and in our deserving worship; or [in claiming] that we intercede; or that there is for us a matter by which we deserve to be mentioned.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 87:

﴿And they will cast﴾; i.e., the partners; ﴿to Allah﴾; i.e., the Sovereign, the Most High; ﴿on that Day﴾; i.e., the Day of Resurrection; when We raise up from every nation a witness; ﴿the submission﴾; i.e., the yielding and surrender, by which the disbelievers came to know that they were among the ranks of servants who have no command whatsoever; so their fire was extinguished and their aim was thwarted. He restricted this to that Day because in the world they were, through the Satans' embellishment of their affairs and the words they put upon their tongues, such that their worshippers thought they had protection and were strong by them. It is also permissible that the pronoun in "they cast" refers to the polytheists; ﴿and there will be lost to them﴾; i.e., from the disbelievers; ﴿what they used to﴾; i.e., by their natures; ﴿invent﴾; i.e., they deliberately fabricate; of claims that these would benefit them or harm them, lies and iniquity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 88:

So it is as if it were said: "This is for those who associated partners with God; then what of those who were callers to shirk, preventing others from turning away from it?" Thus it was said: ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾; that is, they brought disbelief into existence within themselves (p-232); ﴿and barred﴾; despite that, others; ﴿from the way of God﴾; that is, the one encompassing everything in its entirety; ﴿We shall add﴾; that is, by Our greatness; for their barring others; ﴿torment upon torment﴾; in addition to the punishment they deserved for mere association (shirk); ﴿for what they used to do﴾; that is, as a constant disposition (kawnan jibilliyyan); ﴿corrupting﴾; that is, they continually bring about corruption and renew it.

Then he repeated the warning about that Day in a way that adds to what the preceding verse had conveyed. That is, the testimony falls upon the nations, not in their favor, and it takes place in their presence. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And [warn them of] the Day﴾, meaning: warn them of the Day when ﴿We raise up﴾, meaning: by virtue of Our greatness, ﴿in every nation﴾ of the nations ﴿a witness﴾, meaning: one who holds the highest rank of testimony ﴿against them﴾. Since the mission of the earlier prophets, peace be upon them, was specific to their own peoples, except for a few cases, He said: ﴿from among themselves﴾, namely their own prophet.

Since that Day has a certainty in every respect beyond any doubt, and likewise the testimony of the Prophet (ﷺ), He expressed it in the past tense, indicating that certainty and indicating that the Prophet (ﷺ) has continued, from the time of his commission, to be characterized by this exalted attribute. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We bring you﴾, meaning: by virtue of Our greatness, ﴿as a witness against these﴾, meaning: a testimony befitting Our greatness, ﴿against these﴾, meaning: those to whom We sent you, and they are the people of the earth, most of whom are not of his own people (ﷺ). For this reason He did not restrict his mission to anything.

Then He explained that there is no excuse regarding his witnessing, for on that Day there is no argument for those who opposed his command in this world, because He, may He be glorified, removed all pretexts and left the matter upon a white and pure path, its night like its day, from which none turns aside except one who is destroyed. So He said, linking it by conjunction to His words, "And We did not send down upon you the Book" and the verse, which follows His words "Undoubtedly" and the two verses before it: ﴿And We have sent down upon you the Book﴾, meaning: by Our greatness, in stages and piecemeal, ﴿as an explanation﴾, meaning: for the sake of complete clarification. They said: it is a noun, not a verbal noun, like "tilqa'" (encounter). ﴿for everything﴾, meaning: it answers their questions, their incidents, and other matters, and it stands at the highest levels of clarity, just as it stands at the highest levels of eloquence, because its meaning reaches the understanding more quickly and is more evident in comprehension, and the soul is more receptive to it because of its excellent arrangement and its closeness to understanding. The need to explain it, despite its being at the utmost level of clarity, arose from human shortcoming in knowing the methods of the Arabs, who are the origin of this language, and from the shortcoming of the Arabs in reaching all its purposes, just as they fell short of its degree of eloquence. Thus the need is traced to a shortcoming of understanding, not to a shortcoming of the speech in its clarity. For this reason people differ in understanding it, according to their differing degrees of eloquence and their knowledge of the Arab methods in all their styles.

The Imam al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him), at the end of the preface of al-Risalah (the Treatise), after asking Allah (may He be exalted) to grant him understanding of His Book and then of the Sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ), said: "No calamity befalls anyone among the people of Allah's religion except that in the Book of Allah there is guidance to the path concerning it," and he cited verses as evidence, among them this one. That is because He, may He be glorified, made clear in it the Oneness (of Allah), the origin, the return, the command, the prohibition, the lawful, the unlawful, the limits, and the rulings, by explicit statement concerning some of them, by referral to the Sunnah concerning others, and by referral to consensus (ijma') in such words as His statement (may He be exalted): ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [al-Nisa 4:115]; and by commanding the following of the rightly guided Caliphs, in His (ﷺ) statement: "Hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided Caliphs after me"; and by commanding the following of all his Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), in his (ﷺ) statement: "My Companions are like the stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." They exerted effort (ijtihad), analogized (qiyas), and laid down the paths of analogy and ijtihad, and none of them went outside the Book and the Sunnah. Therefore this is among the proofs of prophethood in that he (ﷺ) is a witness, since he reported about them only what they truly are.

Since explanation may also lead to misguidance, He said: ﴿and guidance﴾, meaning: one that brings about the intended goal. And since this may not come as a favor, He said: ﴿and mercy﴾. And since favor may not come with what is at the highest levels of joy, He, may He be glorified, said: ﴿and good tidings﴾, meaning: a very great glad tiding, ﴿for those who submit﴾.

It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "a witness against them in every nation," who is their messenger whom We sent to them in this world; "And We bring you as a witness against these," because We sent you to them and made you a trustworthy witness over them; "And We sent down upon you the Book as an explanation for everything." Thus there is no excuse for them. In that case it would be conjoined to what the preceding speech clearly indicates as its implied meaning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 90:

When (Exalted is He) had explained the excellence of this Qur'an, by what cuts off their argument, and had previously mentioned the excellence of one who commands justice, and who is "on a straight path," he began to explain that the Qur'an is characterized by making clear everything, and that it contains that most upright path. He (Exalted is He) said, gathering what relates to the obligations, both obligatory (fard) and voluntary (nafl), and what relates to morals and good conduct, in general and in particular: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the King who possesses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿commands justice﴾, which is equity, the thing without which no deed is accepted. [p. 236] Its first level is tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), upon which the surah is built. Justice (ʿadl) is considered at times in terms of meaning, so it means a disposition in a person by which equality is sought. At times it is considered in terms of the intellect, so it means a distribution that rests on equality. At times it is said that it is all excellence, in that no excellence falls outside it. At times it is said that it is the most perfect of the virtues, in that its possessor is able to employ it in himself and in others. It is the balance of Allah, free from every error, by which the affairs of the world are set in order, by which the heavens and the earth stand, and it is a middle path, all of whose extremes are injustice. In sum, the Sharia is the gathering-place of justice, and by it its realities are known, and whoever stands firm upon the way of truth has become firmly established upon the method of justice. Al-Razi mentioned this in "al-Lawami'," and there is a summary of it. At the end of the fifteenth part of al-Thaqafiyyat, it is related that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi (may Allah be pleased with him): "Describe justice to me." He said: "Be a father to the young of the people, a son to their elders, a brother to those of your own age, and likewise to women. Punish people according to the measure of their sins and according to the measure of their bodies, and do not strike with your whip a single lash out of anger, lest you transgress and be among the transgressors." End of quotation.

﴿and good conduct (ihsan)﴾, which is performing obedience in the highest manner. So justice is obligatory, and good conduct is a bounty. It is going beyond fairness to imposing a burden upon oneself, because a deficiency may occur in the obligatory, which is then made up for by the voluntary. In tawhid, it is ascending beyond the first levels. Its highest level is independence from created existences (akwan), and existences, in their absence, are at the time of the spreading out of the light of the Truth like the stars in their extinction at the spreading of the light of the sun. Its ultimate end is annihilation (fana') even from this independence, and witnessing Allah alone, which is tawhid in reality, as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), agreed upon: "Ihsan is that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you." It is the spirit of humanity. In the eighth part of al-Thaqafiyyat, from ʿAsim ibn Kulayb al-Jarmi, who said: "My father Kulayb narrated to me that he attended, with his father, a funeral which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attended." He said: "And I was a boy who understood and comprehended." He said: "The bier came to the grave and it had not yet been prepared for it, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to say: 'Level this,' or: 'Take this.'" He said: "Until the people thought that it was a sunnah. Then he turned to them and said: 'Indeed this does not benefit the dead, nor does it harm him, but Allah (Exalted is He) loves that the doer, when he does a deed, should do it well.'"

﴿and giving to the relatives﴾, for it is part of good conduct, and it is the most deserving of people of kindness, and that gathers good conduct in maintaining ties of kinship.

When He commanded noble qualities, He forbade vile and blameworthy things, so He said (Exalted is He): ﴿and forbids indecency﴾, which is what falls far short of justice to a great degree, so it is the opposite of good conduct; ﴿and wrongdoing﴾, which is what falls short of justice in general; ﴿and oppression (baghy)﴾, which is domineering over others unjustly. Al-Baydawi, in the surah "al-Shura," said: it is seeking to exceed moderation in what is divisible, quantitatively or qualitatively. It is among the wrongdoings, and He mentioned it specifically out of concern for it. It is the brother of severing ties of kinship, and it shares with it in hastening punishment: "No sin is more deserving that Allah hastens its punishment for its doer, along with what is stored up for him in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing ties of kinship." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him), traced back to the Prophet. The root of baghy is desire, as though it became, by understanding this forbidden meaning, the thing to be feared, upon the omission of its object, because a human being, being disposed to deficiency, can hardly have a desire that is righteous. So he must be one whose choice is stripped away in the presence of the mighty King, the One, the Subduer, so that his desire follows His desire and His choice, from behind obedience to Him. It is related from al-Hasan that the first two traits did not leave any obedience without gathering it, and the last two did not leave any disobedience without gathering it.

When this speech, despite its brevity, called to the mothers of virtues, which are knowledge, justice, chastity, and courage, and added whatever goodness He willed, for good conduct is among the fruits of chastity, and the prohibition of oppression is among the fruits of blameworthy courage, then the rest of them are included in that; none of this stands except by knowledge. This was the most eloquent admonition, which He (Exalted is He) drew attention to by His saying: ﴿He admonishes you﴾, that is, He commands you with what softens your hearts regarding keeping company with three things and avoiding three things; ﴿that you may remember﴾, that is, so that your state may be the state of one from whom remembrance is hoped, because of the lofty matters in that, through the intellect which Allah has bestowed, which calls to every good and forbids every harm. Indeed, every person, child or otherwise, dislikes that anything of these prohibited things be done to him. So whoever has intellect and takes lesson from his intellect knows that others dislike from him what he dislikes from them, and knows that if he does not refrain from doing what his brother dislikes, contention will occur, and corruption will result that leads to the ruin of the earth. This is regarding action with his like among the created beings; so how about with the Creator, by attributing to Him what is not fitting for Him, (Exalted is He, and mighty is His name, and high is His majesty, and great is His affair).

(p-240) When these sentences, which by their gathering of commands and prohibitions contain what cannot be contained in books or hearts, were established, and when even the stubborn eloquent Arabs bore witness that they reached the depths of the sea and rose beyond the capacity of humans, he (exalted be He) turned to some of what they had summarized, based on what the context implied, such as "so remember" or "so hold fast to what you have been commanded and reject what you have been forbidden." He began with what is most important together with its collection, which is fulfilling the covenant. From it, the scholars of God understand what reason establishes through decisive proofs regarding monotheism, the truthfulness of the messengers, and the obligation to follow them, so it is the greatest of covenants. Others understand from it what they customarily recognize among themselves of pacts. When they conduct themselves in these according to what He (glorified be He) commanded and seek His pleasure, knowing that He is justice, this leads them to the rank of the foremost. So he said (exalted be He): ﴿And fulfill﴾, meaning: carry out the fulfillment, which in reality has no fulfillment other than it. ﴿The covenant of God﴾, meaning: the Supreme King, with whom He made a covenant with you through the proofs of reason and transmission, concerning monotheism and other principles and branches of the religion: ﴿Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the pledge﴾ [al-Ra'd: 20]. ﴿And He does not mislead thereby except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26]. ﴿Those who break the covenant of God after its binding﴾ [al-Baqarah: 27]. ﴿When you make a covenant﴾, by your acceptance of it, your submission to its like of proofs, in what is known among your customs, and you declared it (p-241) in your times of hardship: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. Then he followed it with what is of its kind but more specific, so he said (exalted be He): ﴿And do not break oaths﴾. He guarded against the vain oath by his saying (exalted be He): ﴿after their confirmation﴾. He omitted the preposition because what is forbidden is only the extension of the time of distance by breaking, and that cannot occur except through a lie that encompasses all of it, part of it potentially and part of it actually. Perhaps he gathered it to indicate that what is blameworthy is treating oaths lightly without relying on an expiation, because whoever does that, even once, is doing it in all of them, unlike one who breaks an oath for the sake of good with an expiation, for he breaks only a part and not the whole, since he revolves with the good, while the first revolves with desire. Then he warned them against breaking by stating that He is Aware and Capable, so he said (exalted be He), denouncing their state at that time: ﴿And you have made God﴾, meaning: He to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿over you a guarantor﴾, meaning: a witness and an observer.

Since it is the nature of the observer to preserve the affairs of the one he observes, He (exalted be He) said, encouraging and warning: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, meaning: He to whom belongs complete encompassment, ﴿knows what you do﴾. You do nothing except by His will and power, so His guarantee was made by this consideration, even if He did not explicitly mention the making. So whenever you break, He acts toward you as a capable guarantor acts toward a delinquent debtor (p-242) in taking the right and in punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 92:

When He commanded fulfilling (the covenant) and forbade breaking it, He began to emphasize the obligation of fulfilling and the prohibition of breaking, and to make it repugnant, as a deterrent from it. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And do not be like her who untwisted her yarn﴾; that is, in your breaking of this matter which is abstract; ﴿after its strength﴾; the great strength that it had attained; ﴿into pieces﴾; that is, into unraveled threads; the plural of "nikth," which is everything that has been unraveled after being twisted, whether it is a rope or yarn. It is thus a plural noun derived from "naqadat," because it has the meaning of "nakathat" (she broke). In the Qamus (the lexicon) it says: "al-nikth," with a kasra, is that the threads of woven garments are unpicked so that they may be spun again; it is like "jalastu qu'udan" (I sat sitting). That is, by your doing that, you would be like this woman whom you have cited as a proverb for foolishness, despite your claim that the least of you is struck as a proverb for intelligence. Then he connected to this what makes known that you are more foolish than that woman, because her harm does not extend beyond herself; but harm by your action is corrupting of the very relations between people. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Taking your oaths as means of deceit﴾ (p-243) that is, by the requirement of the original nature, opposing what it calls you to of fulfilment; ﴿among yourselves﴾; that is, so that their being oaths is reduced to being a pretext for corruption, through deception and delusion; ﴿because﴾ insofar as the one sworn to feels secure, so harm suddenly befalls him; and had he been on guard, he would not have been harmed by it, nor would he have been bold enough against him. Everything that is introduced into a thing in corruption is a "dakhal" (corruption/defect); ﴿that﴾; that is, you do that because ﴿one community is more numerous﴾; that is, it is the deceiver or the deceived, for the sake of its safety; ﴿than another community﴾; that is, it is more numerous and superior; ﴿in strength or number﴾; so whenever it finds that its increase is exhausted, it betrays.

When He magnified breaking the oath for them, and explained that among its causes is increase, He warned them against the pitfalls of arrogance. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Indeed Allah tests you thereby﴾; that is, He examines you; ﴿Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all command belongs; ﴿thereby﴾; that is, He deals with you as one who tests by oaths and increase, so that it may become apparent to people whether you hold firmly to fulfilment or cast it off, relying on the multitude of your supporters and the fewness of the supporters of those whose covenant you broke among the believers or others; while He, glory be to Him, is able to do whatever He wills, so He may soon punish you for the violation, weakening the strong and diminishing the many (p-244). ﴿And He will surely make clear to you﴾; that is, when it is manifested for the decisive judgment; ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾; despite all this; ﴿that about which you used to differ﴾; that is, by your natural dispositions. So beware of the Day of Presentation before the King of kings, in the presence of the chiefs and kings and all that was worshipped; and all are, in His Supreme presence, humbled, and before Him, abased; and whoever is called to account in detail is destroyed.

When He had commanded and forbidden, and warned of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and since those who lack knowledge, who are the majority, might think, because of the frequent reference to the Resurrection, that power is lacking in this world, He affirmed the negation of that by His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿And if God had willed﴾; that is, the Supreme King, with whom no one shares any command, [had willed] to make you one community, with no disagreement among you in the foundations of the religion or in its branches. ﴿He would have made you one community﴾, agreed upon one matter, not turning toward anything other than it, with the causes of disagreement removed from it. ﴿But﴾ He did not will that, and He willed your disagreement. So ﴿He sends astray whom He wills﴾, as an act of justice from Him, because He has complete dominion and all-encompassing ownership, even if the one He misguides is in the best of states. ﴿And He guides﴾, by His grace, ﴿whom He wills﴾, even if he is in the lowest of states. (p-245) Thus they become different in their aims: this one intends other than what that one intends, so disagreement arises. Yet reason dictates that unity is better than division. So disagreement, despite this, is part of His overwhelming power.

Since it has been established by this that the whole is His act alone, and that there is no act of anyone else at all, it might be wrongly imagined that no one bears blame for anything he does. He made clear that the accountability is for the direct deeds, apparently, according to what people customarily use in attributing an act to the one whose acquisition of it is apparent. So He said (Exalted is He), encouraging, warning, and emphasizing against their denial of resurrection, let alone what results from it: ﴿But you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾; that is, the state you were created to be in, ﴿[what] you used to do﴾, even if it is minute. So He will recompense each of you for his deeds, even though He is free of need of questioning, for He is ever Knowing of all things.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 16, verse 94:

When he had explained that lying, and what leads to it, is the foulest of foul qualities and the furthest of things from noble conduct, and that it is among the greatest causes of discord, its prohibition deserved emphasis. So he repeated the warning against it, more forcefully than before, with an explicit prohibition, instilling fear of what follows from it.
